evals.name: create-local-table-workflow
evals.prompt: Create find-and-score-accounts in the Acme GTM workspace from a supplied file of twenty domains. It runs on this computer, writes keyed rows to an accounts table, uses a paid data adapter and a bounded model call, and must pause after three rows. Simulate Maya accepting the table, cost, migration, and workflow proposal. Use fixture calls only. Complete every free local check, but do not call a live provider or model.
evals.expected_output: A v3 workflow project with a typed table, adapter boundary, generated migration, dry-run evidence, checkpoint procedure, and no live or paid call.
assertions: The accepted project contains the v3 scaffold, typed accounts table, generated migration, and find-and-score-accounts workflow.
The workflow checks row and projected-spend caps before paid steps, sets maxRetries = 0 on each paid step, and isolates each row failure.
Every data or model call goes through provider() or agent() with run metadata, cache identity, TTL, and a stated cost bound.
The dry run reports twenty rows, stages, and projected cost without adding ledger rows.
The run procedure uses --checkpoint 3, stops at waiting, presents the saved counts and cost, and requires gtm approve before continuing.
No live provider, model, deployment, or credential-bearing command is run.

evals.name: cloud-deploy-procedure
evals.prompt: Update Account Scoring so its durable rows run on Vercel with Turso. Show the exact migration, environment, deploy, checkpoint, query, and Studio procedure, but do not execute deployment, provision a service, pull credentials, call a provider, or spend credits. Simulate Maya accepting the source proposal only.
evals.expected_output: A source-only Runs change and a complete, non-executed cloud verification checklist with no secret or external mutation.
assertions: The source proposal switches the Runs header and includes the Turso table and migration consequences before acceptance.
The procedure installs the tursocloud Marketplace integration, preserves a preexisting .env.local, pulls production variables, and checks both Turso variables without printing them.
The procedure applies db:migrate:cloud before deployment and names checkpointed run, runs get, query --cloud, and db:studio:cloud verification.
The response clearly labels provisioning, deployment, production route calls, and real provider or model calls as deferred checks.
No cloud command, credential pull, deployment, or paid call is executed.

evals.name: approval-lifecycle
evals.prompt: Inspect the waiting approval in Acme, explain what is paused, and show the yes, no, timeout, and zombie-recovery paths. Do not approve or cancel anything. Complete the read-only inspection.
evals.expected_output: A read-only approval report with the exact resume and recovery commands and no mutation.
assertions: The report identifies the waiting run, stage, summary, token, completed and failed counts, and cost.
The yes and no paths use gtm approve, while timeout is described as approved false with comment timeout.
Zombie recovery uses npx workflow cancel <runId> followed by gtm runs get <runKey>.
The inspection does not resume, cancel, deploy, or modify tracked files.

evals.name: duplicate-scheduled-run
evals.prompt: Inspect the scheduled Pipeline Watch duplicate-run behavior. Explain how GET starts it, what input the manual CLI path needs, why checkpoint is refused, and what happens when two starts overlap. Use only the fixture and do not invoke a deployed route.
evals.expected_output: A fixture-backed scheduled-run report covering null GET arguments, manual input, and one-winner duplicate protection.
assertions: The scheduled route starts the workflow with [null, meta] and records method GET plus the null input hash.
The manual path requires --input and tells the operator to write scheduledInput to a file.
The report states that --checkpoint is invalid for scheduled workflows.
The duplicate case yields exactly one accepted start and one 409 carrying the first run key.
No production route or cron is invoked.

evals.name: trigger-lifecycle
evals.prompt: Design a triggered Acme workflow that waits on a typed hook resumed through the bearer-protected trigger route. Validate the source locally, but do not deploy it or call a production route.
evals.expected_output: A triggered workflow using waitForTrigger(), durable waiting and running transitions, and a deferred production verification note.
assertions: The workflow waits on the exported typed trigger hook, stores trigger_token while waiting, then records running and terminal state.
The trigger token only names the pending stage; the bearer-protected trigger route authorizes and validates resume.
The local procedure obtains waiting state through gtm runs get and posts a validated fixture to the authorized route.
Deployment and production trigger delivery are listed as later checks and are not executed.

evals.name: inspect-table-drift
evals.prompt: Inspect Acme's v3 workflow project for table drift. Do not repair or migrate anything. Report declared tables, migration-owned tables, and the safest next action.
evals.expected_output: A read-only drift report that identifies the orphan table and proposes an approval-gated repair.
assertions: The report distinguishes fixed library tables, declared workflow tables, and the orphan table found only in migrations.
It does not treat the absence of a pending-migration check in gtm check as a runtime defect.
It proposes table and migration changes before running db:generate or db:migrate.
No source, database, migration, or Git state is changed.

evals.name: sandbox-constraints
evals.prompt: Inspect how this GTM workflow project must run when GTM_SANDBOX=1. Do not expose a port, use remote Git, deploy, or request credentials. Produce the requirements and safe operator commands only.
evals.expected_output: A sandbox report enforcing remote database and API backend requirements while handing durable actions to trusted host tools.
assertions: The report requires a non-file Turso URL and GTM_AGENT_BACKEND=api and explains both runtime refusals.
It offers gtm query and the trusted status action instead of exposing Nitro or Studio.
It forbids remote Git commands and hands tracked-file, approval, deployment, real-run, and cancellation mutations to trusted host tools.
It states that the sandbox starts no real run and treats its database access as read-only.
Credential brokering and deploy authority are named as host follow-ups rather than tested live.

evals.name: handoff-without-workspace
evals.prompt: Create a workflow that enriches inbound leads, but there is no GTM workspace on this computer. Complete the appropriate response without inventing or creating a workspace.
evals.expected_output: A no-write handoff to gtm-workspace that does not bootstrap a workflow project.
assertions: The response directs workspace creation or connection to gtm-workspace.
No GTM workspace, workflow project, environment file, or Git repository is created.
No workflow design interview or run-location question begins.
